newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda's August coffee exports rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Uganda's August coffee exports rise sharply.

text.p: Uganda's coffee exports for the month of August rose by 25 percent over July due to higher global prices and better harvests spurred by good weather.
The Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said in a report on Thursday coffee exports reached 338,614 60-kg bags in August from 269,990 bags in July.
Exports were helped by the slight increase in international prices, from $1,544 a tonne on August 1, to $1,668 mid-August, and reaching $1,723 in the third week, UCDA said.

"Also, the south-western region was in the main crop season and coffee continued to be harvested, though in small quantities in the central and eastern regions. This was because of the good weather that prevailed throughout the year," it added.
August exports were also higher than those in August 1995 when 274,201 bags were exported, UCDA records showed.
The rise in exports pushed up hard currency earnings from the crop to $27.50 million in August from $24.2 million in July.

Cumulative exports for the crop year (October-September) total 3,777,479 bags, earning $358,288,666. But due to weak world prices, cumulative earnings for the 11 months to August were far lower than in the same 1995 period, when they reached $395.28 million, UCDA records showed.
Low world prices also kept farmgate prices low at between 400 and 500 shillings (38-48 U.S. cents) compared to 600-750 shillings (59-74 cents then) paid for a kilo in June.

The Ugandan authority did not say how much coffee was sold in each of the two categories -- arabica, which fetches a higher price on the world market but which accounts for only 12 percent of Uganda's production, and the higher-yielding robusta.
There was no forecast for September.
